data.content_ref: inline:The target claims that identical stack traces or error codes across diverse nodes indicate a shared latent bug (correlated), while diverse error signatures suggest independent failures. This is a flawed discriminator: a single shared environmental trigger (e.g., leap second) can produce different failure paths and thus diverse error signatures across heterogeneous implementations — the exact scenario the target's own countercondition acknowledges. Conversely, a common library dependency can cause identical stack traces across independently-operated services that genuinely failed independently at the same code point. The Error Signature Diversity test therefore cannot distinguish true independence from apparent uncorrelation; it conflates implementation-path diversity with causal independence, undermining the central evidentiary claim.
